Gardner CNRA:
The proposed street improvements include street resurfacing, reconstruction, curbs, gutters, sidewalks and lights, sanitary sewers and storm drains. These improvements have the potential to injure street root systems and damage grees, as well as necessitate tree removal in some cases. However, if care is exercised during construction work, tree injury and loss can be limited. Further root damage can be minimized by maintaining new street grades as close to old street grades as possible since lowering the street surface would require cutting through many roots and damaging tree root systems. It is not possible to accurately predict the actual loss or injuries until plans for improvements are available.
Mayfair CNRA:
The proposed projects would not adversely impact vegetation or wildlife, although when demolitions are done and new structures move on to the lots, an effort should be made to preserve mature trees when possible. The city has implemented a tree preservation removal ordinance and permit procedure which is intended to preserve large health trees and prevent unnecessary removals.
Northside CNRA:
The proposed sidewalk repairs in the Northside area could cause a loss of some mature street trees where root systems and large roots have to be removed. This would not involve the "Sentinel Tree" on North 21st Street.
Olinder CNRA:
In Olinder, the loans and grants program would not impact the street trees or riparian community.
E. TRANSPORTATION AND TRAFFIC
The range of projects planned for the three-year Community Development Block Grant program will have a negligible impact on traffic volumes or circulation patterns in San Jose. No proposed project involves the widening, extending, or closing of any streets. The CDBG program will not alter existing residential densities or promote residential growth in currently undeveloped areas.
A modest and unmeasureable positive impact may derive from the CDBG efforts to upgrade and preserve older, centrally located neighborhoods. Such a program can make a small contribution to reducing the demand for new housing in outlying residential areas, such as Evergreen and Almaden, which experiences traffic congestion problems due to underveloped circulation networks.
Temporary and minor adverse impacts will result in neighborhoods, primarily Gardner and Alviso, from the disruption of local streets due to the laying of sewer lines and street resurfacing. These activities will require local detours of a temporary nature and will not have a significant or long lasting impact on the neighborhood transportation system.
